title: Adding Acetazolamide on Top of SGLT2 Inhibition in Persons With Type 2 Diabetes
official: Adding Acetazolamide on Top of SGLT2 Inhibition in Persons With Type 2 Diabetes ('DIPPER') Pilot Study
summary: The study aims to determine the acute efficacy and safety of three sequential doses of acetazolamide (62.5 mg, 125 mg, 250 mg) each for 2 weeks in 20 patients with T2D receiving background SGLT2i therapy.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Signed and dated written informed consent.
2. Adult (≥18 years) at the time of consent
3. Established T2D diagnosis as per Diabetes Canada
4. HbA1c ≤10.0%
5. eGFR ≥45 ml/min/1.73m2
6. BP ≤160/90 and ≥90/60 mmHg
7. BMI 18.5-45.0 kg/m2
8. On stable dose of maximally tolerated RAASi for ≥30 days

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Established diagnosis of type 1 diabetes as per Diabetes Canada
2. With known or suspected hypersensitivity or allergy to acetazolamide, dapagliflozin or related products
3. Iodine intolerance
4. Untreated urinary or genital tract infection
5. Serum potassium \<3.5 mmol/L
6. Serum bicarbonate \<22 mEq/L
7. Use of carbonic anhydrase inhibitor in the 30 days prior to screening
8. Liver disease (hepatic cirrhosis, alcohol/drug abuse ≥3 months, or serum AST, ALT, or total bilirubin \>3X the upper limit of normal)
9. Severe glaucoma
10. Acute coronary syndrome, stroke or transient ischemic attack within 30 days prior to screening
11. Active pregnancy, breastfeeding or planning to become pregnant during study period
12. Participation in another drug trial within 30 days of screening
13. Patient not able to understand and comply with study requirements, based on Investigator's judgment.
14. Any other clinical condition that, based on Investigator's judgement, would jeopardize patient safety during trial participation or would affect the study outcome
